cards.claim: Critical batch size for Muon scales inversely with batch size according to a formula involving momentum and weight decay coefficients
cards.conditions: Convergence to gradient-norm threshold in general nonconvex smooth setting; applies to four Muon variants (with/without Nesterov momentum and weight decay)
cards.effect: Lower bound on critical batch size: B_c^* ≥ const × β²σ²/(αη²ε²), where β=momentum, σ²=gradient variance, α=step count, η=learning rate, ε=precision; momentum coefficient β appears as β² in numerator
cards.evidence: Theoretical derivation (Proposition 4.3) with experimental validation on FashionMNIST, CIFAR-10, CIFAR-100 vision tasks and C4 language modeling with Llama3.1 (320M)
cards.quote: We derive a lower bound on the critical batch size for the four Muon variants... For example, for Muon with Nesterov momentum and weight decay we show [B_c^* ≥ (β² σ²)/(α η² ε²)]... it identifies the qualitative scaling law: how the hyperparameters β and λ govern B_c^*, and how the ratio between variants depends only on β and λ (the unknown quantities cancel).

cards.claim: Momentum scaling rule: momentum coefficient β affects critical batch size as β² in the lower bound formula
cards.conditions: All four Muon variants; convergence analysis assumes smoothness and bounded variance conditions
cards.effect: Doubling momentum coefficient increases critical batch size lower bound by 4×; momentum appears squared in CBS formula while weight decay appears linearly
cards.evidence: Theoretical formula (Proposition 4.3) validated empirically on FashionMNIST (MLP), ResNet-18/CIFAR-10, VGG16/CIFAR-100, Llama3.1-320M/C4; includes momentum sweep experiments
cards.quote: For Muon with Nesterov momentum and weight decay we show [formula with β²]. Our experiments validate these hyperparameter-dependent predictions (see Figures 3–4).

cards.claim: Learning rate must satisfy constraint α·η < 1 (product of step count and learning rate less than 1) for convergence with weight decay
cards.conditions: Muon with weight decay; nonconvex smooth optimization
cards.effect: Necessary condition for convergence; for fixed budget (step count α), learning rate η must scale as η ∝ 1/α to maintain convergence
cards.evidence: Theoretical requirement (Theorem 3.2) stated explicitly; experimental validation shown in Figure 1
cards.quote: We also show that for Muon to converge, the learning rate and weight decay coefficient must satisfy λ < α·η, a condition supported by our experimental results (see Figure 1).

cards.claim: Nesterov momentum provides modest convergence improvement but does not change asymptotic rate
cards.conditions: Muon with/without Nesterov momentum; with or without weight decay; general nonconvex smooth setting
cards.effect: Tighter bounds: terms become slightly smaller with Nesterov but asymptotic O(√L/√(αB)) rate unchanged between Nesterov and non-Nesterov variants
cards.evidence: Theoretical comparison of Theorems 3.1(i) vs 3.1(ii) and Theorems 3.2(i) vs 3.2(ii); Proposition 4.3 shows momentum enters critical batch size scaling identically for both variants
cards.quote: Theorem 3.1 shows that Muon, both with and without Nesterov momentum, converges to a neighborhood of a stationary point, and achieves same upper bounds on convergence. Note that some terms in the upper bound are slightly smaller when Nesterov momentum is used.

cards.claim: Weight decay coefficient λ must satisfy λ < 1/(2L) where L is smoothness constant; generally small weight decay values (λ ≪ 1) recommended
cards.conditions: Muon with weight decay; smoothness parameter L; He initialization
cards.effect: Upper bound on weight decay: under He init, L ≈ 2 for conv layers and L ≈ 5 for shortcuts in ResNet-18, allowing λ < 0.25; all experiments use λ ≤ 0.01
cards.evidence: Theoretical requirement from proof technique (Theorem 3.2, Propositions 3.1-3.2); empirically validated—measured L values from ResNet-18 architecture confirm constraint is satisfied in practice
cards.quote: Theorem 3.2 requires that the weight decay coefficient satisfy λ < 1/(2L)... For practical reference, under He initialization the operator norm is for each layer: we measured [values] for convolution layers and for shortcuts in ResNet-18, giving [values]. Hence the condition is satisfied for all weight decay values used in our experiments (λ ≤ 0.01).

cards.claim: Gradient variance σ² (not full gradient dimension) enters the critical batch size bound, potentially much smaller in practice than vector-based optimizers
cards.conditions: Muon in over-parameterized regimes; effective rank r_eff ≪ d (parameter dimension); measured on FashionMNIST MLP
cards.effect: For measured r_eff ≈ 4 vs d = 1024: Muon variance term scales with 4 while SGD scales with 1024, suggesting Muon requires ~256× smaller batch to match SGD's variance contribution; variance reduction factor ≈ d/r_eff
cards.evidence: Theoretical analysis (Theorem 3.1 upper bound depends on r_G_m rather than d); direct measurement in Appendix I on FashionMNIST layer; cited empirical evidence from Ahn et al. (2025) on Llama models up to 3B parameters
cards.quote: The distinguishing feature of Muon's bound lies in the variance term [σ²r_G_m/B], which depends on the rank rather than the full dimension d. Since the SGD-type variance term scales with d while the Muon bound scales with r_G_m, this translates to a variance-term reduction factor of d/r_G_m at fixed B; equivalently, matching Muon's variance contribution would require SGD to use a batch roughly d/r_G_m times larger.

cards.claim: Critical batch size increases monotonically with momentum squared and decreases with weight decay coefficient
cards.conditions: General Muon setting; formulation in Proposition 4.3 uses CBS lower bound formula
cards.effect: CBS ∝ β²/λ when other factors held constant; increasing β increases CBS, increasing λ decreases CBS
cards.evidence: Formula structure in Proposition 4.3; momentum-sweep experiments on C4/Llama3.1 and vision tasks show CBS ordering consistent with β² scaling
cards.quote: Our experiments validate these hyperparameter-dependent predictions (see Figures 3–4). For Muon with Nesterov momentum and weight decay we show [B_c^* ≥ (β² σ²)/(α η² ε²)]... how the ratio between variants depends only on β and λ (the unknown quantities cancel).

cards.claim: Newton-Schulz approximation error decays exponentially with iteration count and has negligible practical impact (~0.01-0.02 pp accuracy loss)
cards.conditions: Practical Muon using Newton-Schulz instead of exact SVD; fixed iteration count used in practice
cards.effect: Approximation error term ε_NS decays exponentially; actual test accuracy gain from exact SVD ≤ 0.01-0.02 percentage points across four widths
cards.evidence: Theoretical bound in Proposition 3.3; experimental comparison across four network widths (Appendix Table 8) showing SVD vs Newton-Schulz equivalence
cards.quote: Since ε_NS decays exponentially with N_S, it is small for the fixed number of Newton-Schulz iterations used in practice, and its impact is therefore limited. In fact, according to Shen et al. (2025), the experimental performance of the SVD-based Muon is equivalent to that of the Newton-Schulz-based version... Our own experiments comparing [iterations] across four network widths (Appendix, Table 8) also show that while [SVD] reduces the approximation error, the test accuracy gain is at most [0.01-0.02] percentage points.

cards.claim: Weight decay provides almost-sure boundedness of parameter and gradient norms without requiring bounded-gradient assumption
cards.conditions: Muon with weight decay; λ < α·η and λ < 1/(2L); no bounded gradient assumption needed
cards.effect: Parameter norm E[||W_t||_op] and gradient norm E[||∇f(W_t)||_F] both almost surely bounded; bounds decrease monotonically with λ and converge as λ → ∞; bounds optimized at λ = 1/(2L)
cards.evidence: Propositions 3.1 and 3.2 with proofs in Appendix C; implies implicit regularization benefit from weight decay beyond convergence rate
cards.quote: Proposition 3.1 establishes that when λ < α·η, weight decay ensures the parameter norm remains almost surely bounded. Furthermore, the upper bound decreases monotonically with λ, converging to 0 as λ → ∞. The bound is minimized uniformly across all t when λ = 1/(2L).

cards.claim: Number of required training steps decreases monotonically and convexly with batch size; critical batch size minimizes SFO complexity
cards.conditions: General convergence framework for Muon; SFO complexity = steps × batch_size
cards.effect: Steps N(B) = Θ(√L/(ε√B)) for convergence to precision ε; CBS exists at B_c^* = argmin(N(B)·B) satisfying Eq. 6
cards.evidence: Propositions 4.1 and 4.2 with formal proofs; establishes existence of unique CBS minimizing computational cost
cards.quote: Proposition 4.1 implies that the required number of steps decreases as B increases... The critical batch size minimizes the computational complexity for training... Proposition 4.2... guarantees the existence of critical batch sizes that are global minimizers of [SFO complexity].
